To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Thyrotropin releasing factor (TRF), which stimulates the secretion of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), also causes an increased secretion of thyroid hormones (TH) in birds.
the thyroid response to thyrotropic hormone releasing hormone is increased in chicks hatched after a temperature treatment during the establishment of hypothalamo hypophyseal thyroid axis.
cold treatment during the period of the establishment of the pituitary thyroid function can have long term effects on the T4 response upon TRH injection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of cold treatment on the pituitary-thyroid axis of the chick embryo and the posthatching chick.
the effect of temperature during pre- and postnatal development on the thyroid function of the domestic fowl and the hypothalamo pituitary control of the thyroid axis.
the development of the thyroid gland in the domestic fowls and the effect of cold treatment on the hypothalamus pituitary thyroid (HPT) axis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a temperature treatment during the establishment of functional pituitary-thyroid axis has a long lasting effect on the T4 response upon TRH injection.
a cold treatment during the period of development of a functional hypothalamo hypophysisal thyroid axis can have a long term effect on the thyroid hormone response to TRH.

the T4 response upon TRH is higher in previously cold treated chickens, but only during the establishment and the first weeks after establishment of a functional hypothalamo pituitary thyroid control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T4 response of the domestic fowl to TRH injection is influenced by the developmental stage of the animal.
the thyroid hormone response to TRH is enhanced by cold treatment during the period of development of the hypothalamus and the pituitary, but not after the pituitary has become fully functional.

cold treatment of the chicken embryo during the establishment of hypothalamic control of thyroid function results in a long lasting enhancement of the T4 response of the thyroid gland to TRH injection, and that this effect is more pronounced when the treatment is applied during the period of establishment of the hypothalamic pituitary control of thyroid function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thyroid hormone response to TRH after cold exposure is developmentally regulated and is dependent on the developmental stage at which the exposure takes place.
cold exposure in the early life of the chicken has a long-lasting effect on thyroid hormone response to TRH.
the T4 response upon TRH injection in 19 day embryos and 1 and 7 day old chickens can be enhanced by a previous cold treatment during days 11 18 of embryonic incubation.
